mcq.QUESTION_DESC: \(\text{The one-dimensional wave equation } \frac{\partial^2 y}{\partial t^2}=c^2\frac{\partial^2 y}{\partial x^2} \text{ is classified as:}\)
\(\text{When using separation of variables for the wave equation, the assumption } y(x,t)=X(x)T(t) \text{ leads to:}\)
\(\text{For a string with zero initial displacement and non-zero initial velocity } g(x), \text{ the general solution is:}\)

mcq.OPT_1: \(\text{Expanding } g(x) \text{ in a Fourier cosine series}\)
mcq.OPT_2: \(\text{Expanding } g(x) \text{ in a Fourier half-range sine series}\)
mcq.QUESTION_DESC: \(\text{If the initial velocity is } g(x)=\lambda x(l-x), \text{ the coefficients } B_n \text{ in the wave equation solution are found by:}\)

mcq.OPT_1: \(C=0 \text{ in the time function } T(t)\)
mcq.OPT_2: \(D=0 \text{ in the time function } T(t)\)
mcq.OPT_3: \(A=0 \text{ in the space function } X(x)\)
mcq.OPT_4: \(B=0 \text{ in the space function } X(x)\)
mcq.QUESTION_DESC: \(\text{In the solution for a string with non-zero initial velocity, applying the initial condition } y(x,0)=0 \text{ leads to:}\)

sq.ANSWER:
Upto the stepMarks

\(\text{Wave equation: } \frac{\partial^2 y}{\partial t^2} = c^2 \frac{\partial^2 y}{\partial x^2}.\)

(1 Mark)

\(\text{Boundary conditions: } y(0,t)=0, y(l,t)=0. \text{ Initial conditions: } y(x,0)=kx(l-x), \frac{\partial y}{\partial t}(x,0)=0.\)

(1 Mark)

\(\text{General solution: } y(x,t)=\sum_{n=1}^\infty B_n \sin\frac{n\pi x}{l} \cos\frac{n\pi c t}{l}.\)

(1 Mark)

\(\text{At } t=0: kx(l-x) = \sum_{n=1}^\infty B_n \sin\frac{n\pi x}{l}.\)

(1 Mark)

\(\text{Fourier sine coefficients: } B_n = \frac{2}{l} \int_0^l kx(l-x) \sin\frac{n\pi x}{l} dx.\)

(1 Mark)

\(\text{Evaluate integral: } B_n = \frac{4kl^2}{n^3\pi^3}[1-(-1)^n].\)

(2 Mark)

\(\text{Hence } y(x,t) = \frac{8kl^2}{\pi^3} \sum_{n=\text{odd}} \frac{1}{n^3} \sin\frac{n\pi x}{l} \cos\frac{n\pi c t}{l}.\)

(1 Mark)
sq.QUESTION_DESC: \(\text{A string of length } l \text{ is fixed at both ends. It is initially displaced into the shape } y(x,0)=kx(l-x) \text{ and released from rest. Find the displacement } y(x,t).\)

sq.ANSWER:
Upto the stepMarks

\(\text{Wave equation: } \frac{\partial^2 y}{\partial t^2} = c^2 \frac{\partial^2 y}{\partial x^2}.\)

(1 Mark)

\(\text{Boundary conditions: } y(0,t)=0, y(l,t)=0. \text{ Initial conditions: } y(x,0)=0, \frac{\partial y}{\partial t}(x,0)=v_0 \sin\frac{2\pi x}{l}.\)

(1 Mark)

\(\text{General solution: } y(x,t)=\sum_{n=1}^\infty B_n \sin\frac{n\pi x}{l} \sin\frac{n\pi c t}{l}.\)

(1 Mark)

\(\text{Differentiate: } \frac{\partial y}{\partial t} = \sum_{n=1}^\infty B_n \frac{n\pi c}{l} \sin\frac{n\pi x}{l} \cos\frac{n\pi c t}{l}.\)

(1 Mark)

\(\text{At } t=0: v_0 \sin\frac{2\pi x}{l} = \sum_{n=1}^\infty B_n \frac{n\pi c}{l} \sin\frac{n\pi x}{l}.\)

(1 Mark)

\(\text{Equate coefficients: } B_2 \frac{2\pi c}{l} = v_0 \Rightarrow B_2 = \frac{l v_0}{2\pi c}, \text{ other } B_n=0.\)

(2 Mark)

\(\text{Hence } y(x,t) = \frac{l v_0}{2\pi c} \sin\frac{2\pi x}{l} \sin\frac{2\pi c t}{l}.\)

(1 Mark)
sq.QUESTION_DESC: \(\text{A string of length } l \text{ is fixed at both ends. Initially in equilibrium, it is given an initial velocity } \frac{\partial y}{\partial t}(x,0)=v_0 \sin\frac{2\pi x}{l}. \text{ Find } y(x,t).\)

lq.ANSWER:
Step Marks
\(\text{Classification: \(A=1\), \(B=4\), \(C=x^2+4y^2\). Discriminant \(\Delta = B^2-4AC = 16 - 4(x^2+4y^2) = 16(1 - (x^2/4 + y^2)).\)}\) (2 Marks)
\(\text{Parabolic: \(\Delta=0\) \(\Rightarrow\) \(x^2/4 + y^2 =1\) (ellipse). Elliptic: \(\Delta<0\) \(\Rightarrow\) inside ellipse. Hyperbolic: \(\Delta>0\) \(\Rightarrow\) outside ellipse.}\) (2 Marks)
\(\text{Vibrating string: \(c=2\) (since \(y_{tt}=4y_{xx}\) \(\Rightarrow\) \(c^2=4\) \(\Rightarrow\) \(c=2\)).}\) (1 Mark)
\(\text{General solution: \(y(x,t)= \sum \sin\left(\dfrac{n\pi x}{5}\right)\left[C_n \cos\left(\dfrac{2n\pi t}{5}\right)+D_n \sin\left(\dfrac{2n\pi t}{5}\right)\right].\)}\) (2 Marks)
\(\text{\(y(x,0)=0\) \(\Rightarrow\) \(C_n=0.\) So \(y(x,t)= \sum D_n \sin\left(\dfrac{n\pi x}{5}\right) \sin\left(\dfrac{2n\pi t}{5}\right).\)}\) (1 Mark)
 

\(\text{\(y_t(x,0)= \sum D_n \left(\dfrac{2n\pi}{5}\right) \sin\left(\dfrac{n\pi x}{5}\right) = 3 \sin(2\pi x) - 2 \sin(5\pi x).\)}\)

 (2 Marks)
\(\text{Compare: For \(n=10\) (since \(\sin(10\pi x/5)=\sin(2\pi x))\): \(D_{10} \left(\dfrac{20\pi}{5}\right)=3\) \(\Rightarrow\) \(D_{10}=\dfrac{3}{4\pi}.\)}\) (2 Marks)
\(\text{For \(n=25\): \(\sin(25\pi x/5)=\sin(5\pi x).\) \(D_{25} \left(\dfrac{50\pi}{5}\right) = -2\) \(\Rightarrow\) \(D_{25} = -\dfrac{2}{10\pi} = -\dfrac{1}{5\pi}.\)}\) (2 Marks)
\(\text{All other \(D_n=0.\) Thus \(y(x,t)= \dfrac{3}{4\pi} \sin(2\pi x) \sin(4\pi t) - \dfrac{1}{5\pi} \sin(5\pi x) \sin(10\pi t).\)}\) (1 Mark)
lq.QUESTION_DESC: \(\text{Classify the PDE: \( u_{xx} + 4u_{xy} + (x^2+4y^2)u_{yy} = e^{x+y}.\)}\\ \text{Determine the regions where it is elliptic, parabolic, hyperbolic.}\\ \text{Also solve the vibrating string problem: \( y_{tt}=4y_{xx}, 00,\)} \text{with \( y(0,t)=0, y(5,t)=0, y(x,0)=0, y_t(x,0)=3 \sin(2\pi x) - 2 \sin(5\pi x).\)}\)

lq.ANSWER:
Step Marks
\(\text{Wave equation: \(c=3\) (since \(c^2=9\)). Length \(l=2\).}\) (1 Mark)
\(\text{General solution: \(y(x,t)= \sum \sin\left(\dfrac{n\pi x}{2}\right)\left[C_n \cos\left(\dfrac{3n\pi t}{2}\right)+D_n \sin\left(\dfrac{3n\pi t}{2}\right)\right].\)}\) (2 Marks)
\(\text{\(y(x,0)= \sin(\pi x) - \sin(2\pi x) = \sin\left(\dfrac{\pi x}{2}\cdot 2\right) - \sin\left(\dfrac{\pi x}{2}\cdot 4\right).\) So \(n=2\) and \(n=4\) terms.}\) (2 Marks)
\(\text{Thus \(C_2=1\), \(C_4=-1\), all other \(C_n=0.\) \(y_t(x,0)=0\) \(\Rightarrow\) \(D_n=0\) for all \(n\).}\) (2 Marks)
\(\text{Hence \(y(x,t)= \sin(\pi x) \cos(3\pi t) - \sin(2\pi x) \cos(6\pi t).\)}\) (1 Mark)
\(\text{Classification: \(A=y^2\), \(B=-2xy\), \(C=x^2.\) Discriminant \(\Delta = 4x^2y^2 - 4y^2x^2 = 0\) for all \(x,y\).}\) (2 Marks)
\(\text{Thus PDE is parabolic everywhere (except possibly where coefficients vanish).}\) (2 Marks)
\(\text{Discuss: parabolic because discriminant identically zero.}\) (2 Marks)
\(\text{Combine results: solution of wave equation and classification of second PDE.}\) (1 Mark)
lq.QUESTION_DESC: \(\text{Solve the boundary value problem: \( \frac{\partial^2 y}{\partial t^2} = 9 \frac{\partial^2 y}{\partial x^2}, 00,\)}\\ \text{with \( y(0,t)=0, y(2,t)=0, y(x,0)= \sin(\pi x) - \sin(2\pi x), \frac{\partial y}{\partial t}(x,0)=0.\)}\\ \text{Also classify the PDE: \( y^2 u_{xx} - 2xy u_{xy} + x^2 u_{yy} + 2u_x - 3u = 0.\)}\\\)
